Three boys of the Xhosa tribe stand next to their tent outside the squatter camp Vukani near Grahamstown, South Africa. According to the culture’s traditions, after their 18th birthday the boys are sent to live on their own outside the village during the winter for one month. They build their own cardboard shelters, wear white face paint and are not allowed to touch anyone or see women for the duration. Upon successful completion, they return to the village to be circumcised and celebrated as men. [Brian Cassella - July 11, 2003]
